steps: Open the refrigerator door fully.
Grip the old bin with both hands and pull it straight out to unsnap it from the door rails.
Align the tabs on the new bin with the door rail slots.
Press firmly until the bin snaps into place.
Test by gently tugging the bin — it should not move.

name: Refrigerator Water Filter
fixes_symptoms: Water tastes bad or has odor

steps: Locate the water filter housing in the upper-right corner of the refrigerator interior.
Turn the old filter counterclockwise about a quarter-turn and pull it straight out.
Remove the cap from the new filter.
Insert the new filter and turn clockwise until it locks.
Run 4 gallons of water through the dispenser to flush the filter before use.
Unplug the refrigerator and turn off the water supply.
Remove the ice bin from the freezer.
Disconnect the wire harness from the old ice maker — press the tab and pull.
Remove the two mounting screws holding the ice maker to the freezer wall.
Slide the old ice maker out and set aside.
Slide the new ice maker into position and secure with the mounting screws.
Reconnect the wire harness until it clicks.
Replace the ice bin, turn on the water supply, and plug in the refrigerator.
Allow 24 hours for the first ice batch to be produced.
Unplug the refrigerator and shut off the water supply valve behind it.
Pull the refrigerator away from the wall to access the rear panel.
Remove the lower rear access panel (typically 2–4 screws).
Place a towel or bucket under the inlet valve to catch residual water.
Disconnect the water supply line from the old valve using pliers.
Unplug the electrical connectors from the valve.
Remove the mounting screws and take out the old valve.
Install the new valve in reverse order — secure screws, reconnect electrical connectors, reattach water line.
Turn on the water supply and check for leaks before pushing the refrigerator back.

tools: Hair dryer (optional, to soften new gasket)
steps: Warm the new gasket in a bucket of hot water for a few minutes to make it pliable.
Open the refrigerator door and locate the gasket — it is pressed into a channel around the door perimeter.
Starting from a corner, pull the old gasket out of the channel.
Work around the door removing the full old gasket.
Press the new gasket into the channel starting from the top corners.
Work around all four sides, ensuring the gasket is seated evenly.
Close the door and check the seal by placing a dollar bill in the door — it should resist being pulled out.

name: Refrigerator Evaporator Fan Motor
fixes_symptoms: Loud or unusual noise from freezer

steps: Unplug the refrigerator.
Empty the freezer and remove all shelves.
Remove the rear freezer panel (usually held by 4–6 screws).
Defrost any ice buildup around the fan motor with a hair dryer on low heat.
Disconnect the fan motor wire harness.
Remove the fan blade by pulling straight off the motor shaft.
Remove the mounting screws and take out the old motor.
Install the new motor and secure the mounting screws.
Reattach the fan blade and reconnect the wire harness.
Reinstall the rear panel, shelves, and plug in the refrigerator.
Pull the old drawer out until it stops, then tilt the front down and lift it free.
Slide the new drawer onto the rails until it is fully seated.
Test by opening and closing the drawer several times.
Unplug the refrigerator and pull it away from the wall.
Remove the lower rear access panel.
Locate the compressor — the start relay plugs into the side of it.
Pull the old relay straight off the compressor terminals.
Shake the old relay — a rattling sound confirms it is faulty.
Plug the new relay onto the compressor terminals until it clicks.
Reinstall the access panel and plug in the refrigerator.
Disconnect power to the dishwasher at the circuit breaker.
Open the dishwasher door and remove the inner door panel screws along the perimeter.
Carefully separate the inner panel from the outer door.
Disconnect the door latch wire harness.
Remove the two screws securing the latch and slide it out.
Install the new latch, secure screws, and reconnect the wire harness.
Reassemble the door panels and restore power.
Test the latch by closing the door — it should click and hold firmly.
Remove the lower rack from the dishwasher.
Twist the spray arm counterclockwise to unlock it from the center hub.
Lift off the old spray arm.
Snap the new spray arm onto the center hub and turn clockwise to lock.
Spin the arm by hand to verify it rotates freely.
Replace the lower rack.
Open the dishwasher door and locate the rubber gasket around the tub opening.
Starting at the top, pull the old gasket out of the channel — it is held by pressure only.
Clean any residue from the channel with a damp cloth.
Press the new gasket into the channel starting at the top center.
Work around all four sides ensuring the gasket sits flush.
Run a short cycle and check for leaks.
Disconnect power at the circuit breaker.
Open the door and remove the inner door panel screws.
Carefully peel back the inner panel to expose the control board.
Take a photo of all wire harness connections before disconnecting.
Disconnect each wire harness by pressing the release tab.
Remove the board mounting screws and lift out the old board.
Install the new board and secure the mounting screws.
Reconnect all wire harnesses per your photo.
Reassemble the door and restore power.
Disconnect power and shut off the water supply.
Remove the lower rack and spray arm.
Unscrew and remove the filter assembly from the tub floor.
Tilt the dishwasher onto its back on towels.
From the bottom, disconnect the pump hoses and wire harness.
Remove the mounting bolts and take out the old pump assembly.
Install the new assembly in reverse order.
Restore the dishwasher to upright, reconnect water, and restore power.
Run a test cycle to confirm no leaks.
Remove the old silverware basket from the lower rack.
Drop the new basket into the same position on the lower rack.
Disconnect power at the circuit breaker.
Remove both dish racks.
The heating element runs along the tub floor — note its orientation.
Tilt the dishwasher onto its back.
From underneath, remove the nuts holding the element terminals through the tub.
From inside the tub, lift out the old element.
Feed the new element terminals through the tub holes and secure the nuts from underneath.
Restore the dishwasher to upright and reinstall the racks.
Restore power and run a drying cycle to test.

name: Dishwasher Detergent Dispenser
fixes_symptoms: Detergent still in dispenser after cycle

steps: Disconnect power at the circuit breaker.
Open the door and remove the inner door panel.
Disconnect the dispenser wire harness.
From the inner door side, remove the mounting screws and push the dispenser out through the outer door.
Insert the new dispenser from the outside, secure mounting screws.
Reconnect the wire harness.
Reassemble the door panel and restore power.
Add detergent and run a cycle to confirm the dispenser opens correctly.
